title: Everyday verbs and saying no
sub: J'ai, je parle, je ne parle pas
can: Say what you have, talk about where you live and what you do, and say no with ne … pas.
doneText: You can now use avoir and the most common -er verbs, and say what you do not have or do not do.

skills.elision: j' and n' before a vowel

discover.intro: Blue sentences say yes. Orange sentences say no. Look at what happens to the verb.
discover.question: What do you notice in the orange sentences?
options: Ne and pas wrap around the verb. Ne becomes n' before a vowel.
The verb moves to the end of the sentence.
The orange sentences use a different verb.
discover.nudge: Not quite. Find the verb in each orange sentence, then look at the words on either side of it.
discover.reveal: To say no, put the verb inside ne … pas. Before a vowel, ne drops to n'. The verbs change their endings too. Most verbs ending in -er follow one pattern:

learn.title: -er verbs and avoir
learn.sub: Tap any form to hear it

blocks.text: Parle, parles and parlent sound exactly the same. The endings -e, -es and -ent are silent. Only nous parlons and vous parlez sound different. So listen for the pronoun.

blocks.title: Un or de
blocks.note: After ne … pas, un, une and des become de (or d' before a vowel): je n'ai pas d'ordinateur. The one exception is être, which keeps the article: ce n'est pas un problème.

blocks.text: Je becomes j' before a vowel or a silent h: j'ai, j'habite, j'aime. Never je ai. The same happens with ne: je n'ai pas, je n'habite pas.
Hunger and cold use avoir, not être: j'ai faim means I'm hungry, and j'ai froid means I'm cold. Literally, I have hunger and I have cold.
Je ne comprends pas is the most useful sentence you will learn. In everyday speech, many French people drop the ne and say je comprends pas. You will hear it, but write it with ne.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means I don't speak English?
exercises.why: Ne goes before the verb and pas goes after it.
J'ai faim: I have hunger, so I'm hungry.

items.why: On takes the same ending as il: -e.

exercises.why: J'habite: je becomes j' before a vowel sound.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.

exercises.why: Je drops to j' before a vowel sound: j'habite.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.why: Je goes with parle, with no s. The s is for tu.
Ne before the verb, pas after it.

exercises.q: To a stranger: do you speak English?
exercises.why: A stranger gets vous, and vous takes -ez.
N'ai pas wraps the verb, and un or des becomes de after it.
After ne … pas, un becomes de: je n'ai pas de frère.
J'habite: je drops to j' before the vowel.

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Tell a new friend where you live, that you speak a little French, and one thing you do not have.
write.starter: J'habite à…  Je parle un peu…  Je n'ai pas de…
write.model: J'habite à Londres. Je parle un peu français. Je n'ai pas de monnaie.
checklist: J'habite with j' before the vowel
Je ne … pas wraps the verb
After pas, un or une becomes de

boss.title: A new friend in a café in Lyon
boss.persona: You are Léo, a friendly student who sits next to the learner in a café in Lyon. Talk about languages, where you live, and food. Address the learner as tu. Keep every message to one short sentence.

choices: Je parle un peu français.
Je parles un peu français.
Je goes with parle, with no s. The s is for tu.
Je ne parle un peu français.
That mixes a yes and a no. You want to say yes: je parle un peu français.

turns.en: Cool. Do you live in Lyon?
choices: Non, je n'habite pas à Lyon.
Non, je ne habite pas à Lyon.
Ne drops to n' before a vowel: je n'habite pas.
Non, je n'habite à Lyon.
A negative needs both parts: ne … pas.

turns.npc: Tu as faim ? Moi, j'ai très faim.
turns.en: Are you hungry? I'm very hungry.
choices: Oui, j'ai faim aussi.
Oui, je suis faim aussi.
Hunger uses avoir: j'ai faim.
Oui, tu as faim aussi.
Tu as means you have. You are talking about yourself: j'ai.
D'accord, on mange ici.
D'accord, on mangent ici.
On takes the same form as il: on mange.
D'accord, on ne mange pas ici.
That means we are not eating here. You said you agree, so keep it positive.
